n: The unconverted — stirred up by Amalekites and Amulonites in Amulon, Helam, Jerusalem, and nearby — grow angry at their converted brothers.
Their hatred becomes so bitter that they reject their king and take up arms against the Anti-Nephi-Lehies.

f.g: Their anger is political as well as religious.

n: The old king passes his kingdom to his son, named Anti-Nephi-Lehi.
The old king dies that same year, as the Lamanites prepare for war.
Ammon and his brothers gather in Midian, then go to Ishmael to counsel with Lamoni and King Anti-Nephi-Lehi about defense.

f.g: A Lamanite land; not the Midian of the Old Testament.

n: Not one convert will take up arms against their brothers or even prepare for war, and the king forbids it.

f.w: would take up arms against their brethren
f.g: A collective decision born of deep repentance.

n: King Anti-Nephi-Lehi speaks. He thanks God for sending Nephite missionaries to show them their fathers’ wicked traditions.

f.g: He begins with gratitude, not fear.

n: He thanks God for softening their hearts and opening friendship with the Nephites.
Through this contact they came to see their sins, including many murders.

f.w: the many murders which we have committed
f.g: Their past violence weighs heavily on them.

n: He thanks God for allowing them to repent and for forgiving them — removing guilt from their hearts — through the merits of his Son.

f.w: through the merits of his Son

n: They were “the most lost of all mankind,” and it took everything they had to repent enough that God would remove their stain.
Since God has made their swords bright again, let us never stain them with our brothers’ blood.

f.g: A powerful image: clean swords stand for cleansed souls.

n: If they stained them again, perhaps they could never again be washed clean by the blood of God’s Son. They fear falling back into sins already forgiven.

f.w: they can no more be washed bright

n: God revealed all this in advance because he loves their souls as much as their children’s, sending angels to make the plan of salvation known.

f.w: he loveth our souls as well as he loveth our children

n: “Oh, how merciful is our God!” Let us hide our bright swords as a testimony at the judgment that we never stained them again.

f.w: Oh, how merciful is our God

n: If attacked, they will bury their swords deep in the earth as a witness that they never used them — and if killed, they will go to God and be saved.

f.w: we will bury them deep in the earth
f.g: The origin of the phrase about burying weapons; compare Isaiah’s swords beaten into plowshares.

n: The people bury all their weapons used for shedding blood deep in the earth.

f.w: they did bury them up deep in the earth

n: It was a covenant before God and man: they would die rather than kill, give rather than take, and work hard rather than live idly.
Mormon’s lesson: once converted, these Lamanites were firm, choosing death over sin. They buried their weapons of war for peace.
The hostile Lamanites march to the land of Nephi to depose the king and destroy his people.

f.w: to place another in his stead
f.g: A coup against the converted king.

n: The converts go out to meet them, lie face down, and pray — and the attackers start killing them.

f.g: Lay face down in total nonresistance.

n: Meeting no resistance, the attackers kill 1,005. Mormon is confident they are blessed and with God.

f.g: Mormon preserves the exact number of these martyrs.

f.w: gone to dwell with their God

n: The attackers see the converts neither fleeing nor fighting, but praising God as they die.

f.w: praised God even in the very act of perishing

n: The attackers stop. Many are heartbroken for those they killed and repent.
They throw down their weapons, stung by guilt, and lie down with the converts, trusting the mercy of those who had just been their victims.
More people join the church that day than were killed. The slain were righteous, so we can trust they were saved.

f.w: joined that day by more than the number who had been slain
f.g: Out of tragedy, more souls were gained than lost.

n: No wicked person was killed, yet over a thousand came to the truth. The Lord works in many ways to save his people.

f.w: the Lord worketh in many ways

n: Most of the attackers were Amalekites and Amulonites of the order of Nehor.
None of the new converts were Amalekites, Amulonites, or Nehorites — they were true descendants of Laman and Lemuel.

f.w: actual descendants of Laman and Lemuel

n: Mormon draws a solemn lesson: people who once had great spiritual light and then fall away become harder than if they had never known the truth.
